source: Hand-curated by planet-hunter (skyspectra) from the cited papers' own abstracts (arXiv / publisher pages); bibliographic data checked against Crossref.
credit: Each detection credits its paper (reference.title, authors, journal, DOI). Compiled 2026-09-26.
licence: Compilation: CC0 1.0 (facts with citations). abstract_quote fields are short verbatim excerpts quoted for attribution; copyright remains with the authors/publishers.
method: Every abstract_quote was copied from the paper's own abstract. For papers with an arXiv ID this is the arXiv abstract (read through the arXiv API, which returns the same text as https://arxiv.org/abs/<id>); for Vidal-Madjar et al. 2003 it is the nature.com publisher page. LaTeX markup in quotes is rendered as plain text (e.g. H$_2$O -> H2O, $\sigma$ -> sigma); otherwise the wording is verbatim. arXiv abstracts can differ slightly from the final published abstracts. Titles, journal, volume, first page and DOI were checked against Crossref metadata for each DOI.
status_rules: detected = claimed in the abstract without hedging; tentative = abstract hedges (evidence/possible/potential/likely) or the curator notes why; contested = a later peer-reviewed paper disputes it (cited in note).
ads_caveat: ADS pages (ui.adsabs.harvard.edu) returned a CAPTCHA 'Human Verification' page and could not be read. The ADS bibcodes were built from the Crossref-verified year/journal/volume/page/first-author initial using the standard ADS bibcode format, but were NOT loaded and confirmed on ADS. Please spot-check them, or use the DOI links instead.

reference.title: Identification of carbon dioxide in an exoplanet atmosphere
reference.authors: JWST Transiting Exoplanet Community Early Release Science Team et al.

detections.abstract_quote: Here we present the detection of CO2 in the atmosphere of the gas giant exoplanet WASP-39b from transmission spectroscopy observations obtained with JWST as part of the Early Release Science Program (ERS). The data used in this study span 3.0 to 5.5 μm in wavelength and show a prominent CO2 absorption feature at 4.3 μm (26σ significance).

detections.abstract_quote: We robustly detect multiple chemical species at high significance, including Na (19σ), H2O (33σ), CO2 (28σ), and CO (7σ).

reference.title: Detection of an Extrasolar Planet Atmosphere

detections.note: Contested: Casasayas-Barris et al. 2020, 'Is there Na I in the atmosphere of HD 209458b? Effect of the centre-to-limb variation and Rossiter-McLaughlin effect in transmission spectroscopy studies' (A&A 635, A206; doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201937221) find with HARPS-N/CARMENES that 'the transmission spectrum reveals no detectable NaI absorption in HD 209458b' and say earlier pioneering studies 'may have overlooked' CLV and RM effects. Their data are ground-based high-resolution, while Charbonneau used HST/STIS low-resolution photometry, so the dispute is about the Na signal in general and does not directly re-reduce the HST data.
detections.abstract_quote: We interpret this additional dimming as absorption from sodium in the planetary atmosphere, as recently predicted from several theoretical modeling efforts.

reference.title: JWST-TST DREAMS: Quartz Clouds in the Atmosphere of WASP-17b

detections.abstract_quote: Our transmission spectrum shows additional opacity centered at 8.6 μm, and detailed atmospheric modeling and retrievals identify this feature as SiO2(s) (quartz) clouds. The SiO2(s) clouds model is preferred at 3.5-4.2σ versus a cloud-free model and at 2.6σ versus a generic aerosol prescription.

reference.title: Water vapour in the atmosphere of the habitable-zone eight-Earth-mass planet K2-18 b

detections.note: Contested: Bezard et al. 2022, 'Methane as a dominant absorber in the habitable-zone sub-Neptune K2-18 b' (Nature Astronomy 6, 537; doi:10.1038/s41550-022-01678-z) argue the 1.4 micron HST/WFC3 feature 'is most likely due to methane' and is 'not diagnostic of the presence of water vapour' for sub-Neptunes below about 600 K. JWST (Madhusudhan et al. 2023) then detected CH4. (arXiv abstract text contains the macro '\planet\' in place of 'K2-18 b'; it has been replaced in the quote.)
detections.abstract_quote: Here we report the detection of an H2O spectroscopic signature in the atmosphere of K2-18 b -- an eight M⊕ planet in the habitable-zone of an M-dwarf -- with high statistical confidence (ADI = 5.0, ∼3.6σ).

detections.abstract_quote: Here, we report the detection of water vapor and the likely presence of liquid and icy water clouds in the atmosphere of the 2.6 R⊕ habitable-zone planet K2-18b.

detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum reveals strong detections of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at 5σ and 3σ confidence, respectively, with high volume mixing ratios of ~1% each in a H2-rich atmosphere.

reference.title: Carbon-bearing Molecules in a Possible Hycean Atmosphere

detections.note: Contested: Schmidt et al. 2025, 'A Comprehensive Reanalysis of K2-18 b's JWST NIRISS+NIRSpec Transmission Spectrum' (AJ 170, 298; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae019a) confirm CH4 (about 4 sigma) but 'find no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO2 or DMS'.
detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum reveals strong detections of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at 5σ and 3σ confidence, respectively, with high volume mixing ratios of ~1% each in a H2-rich atmosphere.

reference.title: Carbon-bearing Molecules in a Possible Hycean Atmosphere

detections.note: Tentative in the original abstract ('potential signs of dimethyl sulfide'), and later contested. Schmidt et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 298; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae019a) find 'no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO2 or DMS'. Luque et al. 2025, 'Insufficient evidence for DMS and DMDS in the atmosphere of K2-18 b. From a joint analysis of JWST NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations' (A&A 700, A284; doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202555580) state 'there is no statistical significance for DMS or DMDS in K2-18 b's atmosphere'.
detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum also suggests potential signs of dimethyl sulfide (DMS), which has been predicted to be an observable biomarker in Hycean worlds, motivating considerations of possible biological activity on the planet.

TRAPPIST-1 b.note: No atmospheric species detected. Greene et al. 2023, 'Thermal emission from the Earth-sized exoplanet TRAPPIST-1 b using JWST' (Nature 618, 39; doi:10.1038/s41586-023-05951-7; ADS 2023Natur.618...39G; arXiv:2303.14849), JWST MIRI F1500W: 'The most straightforward interpretation is that there is little or no planetary atmosphere redistributing radiation from the host star and also no detectable atmospheric absorption from carbon dioxide (CO2) or other species.' Lim et al. 2023, 'Atmospheric Reconnaissance of TRAPPIST-1 b with JWST/NIRISS: Evidence for Strong Stellar Contamination in the Transmission Spectra' (ApJL 955, L22; doi:10.3847/2041-8213/acf7c4; ADS 2023ApJ...955L..22L; arXiv:2309.07047), JWST NIRISS SOSS: 'we confirm the absence of cloud-free hydrogen-rich atmospheres, but cannot assess the presence of secondary atmospheres.'

reference.title: A reflective, metal-rich atmosphere for GJ 1214b from its JWST phase curve

detections.note: Tentative: the abstract says '>3σ evidence of absorption features, with H2O as the most likely cause'. The lead said this paper suggested possible CO2, but its abstract names only H2O and a 'high metallicity atmosphere'.

reference.title: Possible Carbon Dioxide above the Thick Aerosols of GJ 1214 b

detections.note: Tentative: the title says 'Possible' and the abstract says 'more observations are needed to confirm the carbon dioxide and methane signatures'.
detections.abstract_quote: Here, we present a JWST NIRSpec transmission spectrum from 2.8 to 5.1 um that shows signatures of carbon dioxide and methane, expected at high metallicity. A model containing both these molecules is preferred by 3.3 and 3.6 sigma as compared to a featureless spectrum for two different data analysis pipelines, respectively.

GJ 1214 b.note: Classic result with no species: Kreidberg et al. 2014, 'Clouds in the atmosphere of the super-Earth exoplanet GJ 1214b' (Nature 505, 69; doi:10.1038/nature12888; ADS 2014Natur.505...69K; arXiv:1401.0022), HST WFC3: 'The observed spectrum, however, is featureless. We rule out cloud-free atmospheric models with water-, methane-, carbon monoxide-, nitrogen-, or carbon dioxide-dominated compositions at greater than 5σ confidence.'

detections.abstract_quote: Here we present an optical transmission spectrum for the 'hot-Saturn' WASP-96b obtained with the Very Large Telescope, which exhibits the complete pressure-broadened profile of the sodium absorption feature.

WASP-96 b.note: Radica et al. 2023 (MNRAS 524, 835; doi:10.1093/mnras/stad1762; arXiv:2305.17001) is not listed as a detection. Its abstract gives only metallicity (1-5x solar) and solar C/O, plus a short-wavelength slope that 'could either be caused by enhanced Rayleigh scattering or the red wing of a pressure-broadened Na feature'.

not_included: WASP-121 b: Evans-Soma et al. 2025 (JWST, SiO) was not found through arXiv search and its abstract could not be read, so it is dropped.
WASP-39 b: the ERS CO2 paper also 'tentatively detect[s] a small absorption feature near 4.0 μm'. No species is named in that abstract (it was later attributed to SO2), so it has no separate entry.

GJ 1214 b: the lead 'Kempton et al. 2023 possible CO2' was corrected. The Kempton abstract names only H2O (tentative) and a metal-rich atmosphere. The possible CO2 is from Schlawin et al. 2024 (ApJL 974, L33).
WASP-96 b: the lead 'Radica et al. 2023: H2O, CO2?' was corrected. Radica's abstract claims no species, and the H2O/CO2/K constraints come from Taylor et al. 2023.

HD 209458 b: the lead said Casasayas-Barris et al. 2020 disputes Charbonneau's HST sodium. Its abstract disputes Na I in ground-based high-resolution data and says earlier studies may have overlooked CLV/RM effects. It does not re-analyse the HST data. It is kept as the 'contested' reference with this caveat.
All ADS bibcodes: built from verified metadata but not loaded on ADS, because of a CAPTCHA (see meta.ads_caveat).
Fu et al. 2024: the instrument (NIRCam) is not stated in the abstract (see planet note).
